Subject: Post-call recap & pricing options — FintechAI (latency vs cost)

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: real-time customer chat + short-form summarization for compliance workflows. ~50M tokens/month expected (peak bursts during US business hours).
- Latency SLOs: user-facing chat: p95 <= 300 ms; key flows (KBA retrieval + response): p95 <= 200 ms. Background/async jobs can tolerate ~1s+.
- Quality: want to keep model fidelity; open to quantized variants if perf/cost tradeoffs hold.

Budget & target unit economics you mentioned on the call:
- Existing budget range: $400k–$800k/year for inference (incl. embeddings and chat).
- Target $/1M tokens you referenced: roughly $250–$350 (goal to hit this with a mixed deployment).

Initial options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted Standard (cost-optimized): batching + prefix caching. Lower unit cost, higher tail latency (p95 often 300–500ms for bursts).
2) Hosted Premium (latency-optimized): streaming + reserved warm pools. Higher cost per token but better p95.
3) Dedicated (reserved capacity): best predictable latency and unit economics at scale if you commit to sustained tokens (especially for hot routes).

Suggested next steps:
- I attached our latest pricing sheet (redwood-pricing-v2.pdf) and a 2-week pilot SOW template (FTAI-pilot-sow.docx).
- If you can confirm target monthly token mix (percent real-time vs background) I can run a projected unit economics table for the three options and propose a pilot config (dedicated for 50–60% of hot routes + hosted for burst/async).

Would you be able to share a typical token distribution (e.g., % of sessions, avg tokens per session) by EOD Friday? If not, a best-effort estimate works, and we can iterate.

Thanks —
Marissa

Alex — thanks for the details, this helps a lot. Below is a concise unit-econ projection and deployment recommendation based on your mix (50M tokens/mo, 65% real-time):

Option A — Hosted Standard (batching/caching)- Unit cost example: ~$400 / 1M tokens (blended)- Latency: p95 typically 300–500ms under bursts (may miss your 300ms p95 for chat)

Option B — Hosted Premium (streaming + warm pools)- Unit cost example: ~$700 / 1M tokens (blended)- Latency: p95 ~150–250ms for chat; better tail behavior

Option C — Dedicated (reserved GPU pools)- Committed pricing example: $200–$300 / 1M tokens effective with annual commit (depends on model size, quantization)- Latency: p95 < 150ms consistently; best for critical user-facing routes

Blended recommendation to meet your goals (target $250–$350 / 1M):
- Pilot config: dedicate capacity for 50–60% of hot chat traffic (critical flows) and route the rest to Hosted Standard with prefix caching and batching for background jobs. This gives predictable low latency on hot routes while keeping blended unit cost near your target.

Notes on controls you can use to trade latency vs cost:
- Batch window sizing: small windows (10–50ms) increase batching efficiency but can add tail latency; tune per-route.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming reduces first-token latency and perceived responsiveness but often increases compute (higher token overhead) — cost delta typically 20–50% depending on model.
- SLO-driven routing: route calls tagged as "critical" to Premium/Dedicated and others to Standard. We can enforce via API flags and routing policies.

Next steps I propose:
1) We share an initial pilot SOW and set up a two-week traffic mirror for one chat flow.
2) Engineering (Dev) will propose batch window defaults and instrumentation to capture p95/p99 and token counts.
3) Pricing: I can model a 3-scenario projection (Conservative, Target, Aggressive) showing blended $/1M across months and the break-even commit for Dedicated.

Can I book a brief 30-min follow-up early next week to walk through the pilot SOW and the three-scenario pricing model?

Thanks —
Marissa
